title: 2 Mathematics KCPE 2004
text:
THE KENYA NATIONAL EXAMINATION COUNCIL
 KCPE 2004
 MATHEMATICS Time:2 hours
 READ THE INSTRUCTION CAREFULLY
 1. You have been given this question booklet and a separate answer sheet. The question booklet
 contains 50 question
 2. Do any necessary work in this booklet.
 3. When you have chosen your answer, mark it on the ANSWER SHEET, not in this question
 booklet
 HOW TO USE THE ANSWER SHEET
 4. Use only ordinary pencil.
 5. Make sure that you have written on the answer sheet:
 YOUR INDEX NUMBER
 YOUR NAME
 NAME OF YOUR SCHOOL
 6. By drawing a dark line inside the correct numbered boxes mark your full index number (i.e.
 school code number and three figured candidate’s number) grid near the top of the answer
 sheet.
 7. Do not mark outside the boxes.
 8. Keep the sheet as clean as possible and do not fold it.
 9. On the answer sheet the correct answer is to be shown by drawing a dark line inside the box in
 which the letter have chosen is written
 Example
 In the question booklet :
 10. What is the next number in the pattern:
 1.2, 2.4, 4.8,______?
 A. 6.0
 B. 7.2
 C. 8.4
 D. 9.6
 On the answer sheet:The correct answer is D

 8 15 11 9 17 14 12 14 13
 10 18 8 9 16 13 13 10 12

 12. A bag of sugar weighed 108.5kg. Mwangi bought 16 bags. He then removed 0.3kg of sugar from
 each bag. What total weight of sugar remained?
 A. 1736kg
 B. 108.2kg

 A. 3:2
 B. 2:300
 C. 3:200
 D. 200:3
 14. One hundred and twenty litres of juice is packed in two deciliters packets. How many packets
 are needed?
 A. 60
 B. 600
 C. 6000
 D. 60000
 15. Musa bought the following items from a kiosks:
 3kg of tomato
 ½ kg of onion @sh. 30
 2kg packets of maize flour for sh. 38
 ½ kg of sugar @ sh. 44
 He paid for the items using a sh. 200 note. How much balance did he get?
 A. Sh. 50
 B. Sh. 150
 C. Sh.63
 D. Sh. 12
 16. What is the value of 24÷ 3+ 4 x 5 - 8÷4 x 10 +1?
 A. 7
 B. 9
 C. 41
 D. 131
 17. The table below shows the cost in shillings of sending parcels through the post.
 Weight steps Africa Europe Near East Rest of the wold
 Up to 1 kg 940.00 1030.00 1070.00
 Over 1kg up to 3kg 1335.00 1390.00 1455.00

 20. The marked price of an article was sh. 300. Ali paid sh. 260 for the article after being given a
 discount. What percentage discount did he get?
 A. 86 2/3%
 B. 40%
 C. 15 5/13%
 D. 13 1/3 %
 21. The figure below represents a vegetable garden bounded by two semi –circle, 5 m apart. The
 diameter of the lager semi-circle is 30m.
 What is the perimeter of the garden?
 A. 78.50m
 B. 88.50m
 C. 83.50m
 D. 96.35M
 22. Asha was given a loan of sh. 48 000. She repaid the loan after two years with compound interest
 at rate of 25% p.a.How much money did she pay altogether?
 A. Sh. 60 000
 B. Sh. 63 000
 C. Sh.72 000
 D. Sh.75 000
 23. What is the square root of 1 7/9?
 A. 4/9
 B. 8/9
 C. 1 1/3
 D. 3 13/81

 and angle NRM = 420

 A. 1120
 B. 680
 C. 440
 D. 700
 25. A saleswoman was paid a monthly salary of sh. 9000. She was also paid a commission of 10%
 for all the goods she sold above sh. 10 000. In one month she sold goods worth sh. 25 000
 What did she earn at the end of that month?
 A. Sh. 11 500
 B. Sh. 12 500
 C. Sh. 10 500
 D. Sh. 1 500

 the balance in equal numbers of sh. 200 and 100 notes.
 What total numbers of notes did he receive?
 A. 6
 B. 5
 C. 4
 D. 3
 28. The table below shows the number of tonnes of sugar produced and sold by a factory in 6 days
 On which was the number of tonnes of sugar sold one and half times the number of tonnes
 produced?
 A. Thur
 B. Mon
 C. Wed
 D. Sat
 29. The number of patients who visited a health centre on Monday was 125, on Tuesday was 163
 and on Wednesday was 210.
 On Thursday the number was 15 less than those who visited on Wednesday. Equal number of
 patients visited the centre on Friday and Saturday. The total number of patients visited the
 centre in six days
 How many patients visited the centre on Friday?
 A. 396
 B. 288
 C. 183
 D. 198
 30. The area of the curved surface of cylinder is 6160 cm 2 The length of cylinder is 10cm.
 What is the radius of the cylinder in centimeters?
 (Take π 22/7)
 A. 98
 B. 14
 C. 196
 D. 968
 31. The table below shows Mwasi’s income from the sale of farm produce,during one year. The
 information on the income for potatoes is not given.
 A pie chart was drawn to represent the information above. If the angle representing the income
 for beans was 630 What was the income for the potatoes?
 A. Sh. 120 000
 B. Sh. 18 000
 C. Sh. 17 850
 D. Sh. 102 000
 32. A bus left Migori town for Nairobi at 19 00h. It arrived in Nairobi 9 hours later. At what time did
 the bus arrive in Nairobi?
 A. 3.00p.m
 B. 3.00 a.m
 C. 4.00p.m
 D. 4.00 p.m
 33. According to survey, three antelopes die every five minutes whereas four are born every
 minute. What is the difference between the number of antelopes that are born and those that
 die in one day?
 A. 48 96
 B. 1440
 C. 5760
 D. 2448
 34. Construct the triangle JKL such that JK=JL=5.5cm and KL = 7cm. Draw the bisector of the angle
 KJL to meet line KL at M.
 Which one of the following statements is correct from the construction?
 A. Triangle JML is an isosceles triangle
 B. Triangle JKL is the Right angled.
 C. Line JM is perpendicular to KL
 D. Angle JKL =450
 35. The hire purchase price of a T.V set is 40%more than the cash price. The cash price is sh. 20 000
 Ochieng paid sh. 2100 as a monthly instalment for 10 months.
 How much had he paid as deposit?
 A. Sh. 8 000
 B. Sh. 13 000
 C. Sh. 1 000
 D. Sh. 7 000
 36. A factory hires 12 workers to complete a piece of work in 5 hours. If two of the workers do not
 turn up, how will it take to complete the work?
 A. 60h
 B. 30h
 C. 24h
 D. 6h

 T U

 40. A shopkeeper bought 5 trays of eggs at sh. 120 per tray. Ten eggs broke and she sold the rest at
 sh. 6 per egg.
 If a tray holds 30 eggs, what percentage profit did she make?
 A. 50%
 B. 40%
 C. 28 4/7 %
 D. 240%
 41. Muli spent ¾ of his salary on food and 2/5 on rent. He was left with sh. 2100.
 What was his salary?
 A. Sh. 3000
 B. Sh. 3675
 C. Sh. 4900
 D. Sh. 7000
 42. Mambo took 30 minutes to cycle from home to the market at an everage speed of 5 metres per
 second. After staying at the market for 20 minutes, he cycled back and took 25 minutes to reach
 home. What was the average speed, in metres per second for the whole journey?
 A. 5 5/11 metres per second
 B. 4 metres per second
 C. 2 metres per second
 D. 6 metres second
 43. One cuboid measures 2m by 4m by 3m. Another cuboid measures 10cm by 8cm by 5cm.
 What is the difference in their volumes in cubic metres?
 A. 23.6
 B. 23. 96
 C. 23.996
 D. 23.9996
 44. A shopkeeper bought a shirt for sh. 300. He then sold it for sh. 360 after giving a discount of 10%
 What percentage profit would he have made if no discount was given?
 A. 33 1/3 %
 B. 27 7/9%
 C. 25%
 D. 20%

 (Takeπ 22/7)

 the number of oranges. The number of mangoes was twice the total number of oranges and
 pawpaws.
 The total number of fruits bought was 48.If the of oranges was x,which of the equation below
 can be used to find the number of oranges bought?
 A. 3x + 24 =48
 B. 6x +16=48
 C. 6x +24=48
 D. 4x +16 =48

 Two crates of 300ml @sh. 415
 Three crates of 500ml @sh. 563
 Five crates of one litres @sh. 415
 He then spent sh. 50 on transport. If he had five thousand shillings ,how much money did he
 remain with?
 A. Sh. 356
 B. Sh. 406
 C. Sh. 3557
 D. Sh. 4644

 Which one of the graphs represents the cyclist’s journey?
